decisions.rationale: Measurement, ARCHITECTURE.md:1970-1978: keeping D-101's constraint made correct inverted readings unreachable, and extending the two helper predicates to augmented and half-diminished was 'the largest single improvement of iteration path 1'.

decisions.title: Pedal-point detection is a second pass, accepted only on two conditions
decisions.verbatim:
**Pass 2** is triggered only when the Pass 1 bass PC is NOT a chord tone of the
winner.
decisions.plain: When the lowest note does not belong to the chord the upper voices spell, the program re-analyses without it. It accepts that reading only if the upper voices give at least two different pitch names and the answer is clearly better than the next different-rooted one.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3652-3682 'Status: Implemented (Session 18, master fb9a27ce9a)'. Suspended on the record arm - see D-021. SUPERSEDED BY D-207 - open_items/OI-194.md:7 records the ratified successor (user, 2026-07-26): the voice-independent pedal-point class replaces this bass-only second pass and the `isPedalPoint`/`pedalBassPc` fact it produces
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:3656-3661: a single pass over an organ point either forces a bass-root reading and suppresses the upper-voice harmony, or returns a slash chord with the wrong root when a template accidentally fits. The 'different-root competitor' detail carries its own recorded reason at :3640-3643 - several templates share a root, so a gap measured against rank 2 collapses to about 0.047 and blocks detection for bare triads.

decisions.title: The bass-is-root bonus is conditioned on corroborating support
decisions.verbatim:
`bassNoteRootBonus` is now conditioned on corroborating root-position support in the
accumulated tones:
decisions.plain: Being the lowest note no longer counts as strong evidence of being the chord's root unless the chord above actually supports that reading. Without a third or fifth above it, the bonus almost vanishes.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3439-3487; the failure it fixed is documented across four corpora at :3406-3419
decisions.rationale: Measurement, ARCHITECTURE.md:3444-3463: four corpora (Chopin mazurka, Mozart sonata, Corelli trio sonata, Beethoven quartet) were inspected at the score and found to share ONE mechanism - the bass moves faster than the harmonic rhythm, so each bass note independently takes the bonus and overrides the root the chord tones above already identify. The fix conditions the bonus on corroborating root-position support rather than shrinking it.

decisions.title: The spelling written in the score is read through ONE shared interpreter
decisions.verbatim:
read through the **shared** `engravingbridge::lineOfFifths` primitive (the Layer-1.5 spelling
  view) — one interpreter, not a per-layer tpc copy.
decisions.plain: How a note is spelt on the page - F sharp versus G flat - is interpreted in one shared place, not re-implemented by each stage that needs it.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1210-1213. ARCHITECTURE.md:1221-1225 records the unification residual: the legacy scorer still carries its own second reader until the legacy path retires
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1211-1213 - 'one interpreter, not a per-layer tpc copy' (#6): two interpreters of the notated spelling can disagree, and open_items/OI-173 records what that costs when it happens (four inequivalent definitions of the same predicate).

decisions.title: The augmented-sixth labels are gated to the Standard and Baroque presets
decisions.verbatim:
Gated to
Standard and Baroque presets only. Jazz and Nashville presets continue to
emit chromatic Roman numerals or chord symbols respectively.
decisions.plain: The specific Italian, French and German augmented-sixth labels are shown only under the classical presets.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-112 already records this preset-gating as stale; open_items/OI-201 records that the record arm collapses the family to a plain major triad symbol

decisions.title: American English throughout
decisions.verbatim: All identifiers, comments, and documentation use American English spelling.
decisions.plain: Analyzer, not analyser; color, not colour.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:440-450; restated in CLAUDE.md Conventions
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:440-450: MuseScore's own codebase is American English, so one spelling convention throughout is what keeps identifiers matching across the boundary.

decisions.title: Cross-platform by default
decisions.verbatim:
All code must run on every platform officially supported by MuseScore Studio: Windows,
macOS, and Linux.
decisions.plain: Everything must work on Windows, macOS and Linux; platform-specific code is allowed only where unavoidable and must be walled off.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:624-630
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:624-630: the code must run on every platform MuseScore Studio officially supports, so platform-specific code is permitted only when unavoidable and must be abstracted so the rest of the module stays platform-agnostic.

decisions.title: The open-items register is the one home for every unresolved issue, and the index is the status of record
decisions.verbatim:
this file is the complete INDEX and
> the **authoritative status surface**
decisions.plain: Every known unresolved problem has exactly one row in one file, and that row - not the longer write-up beside it - is the official statement of where it stands.
decisions.status_source: OPEN_ITEMS.md:3-13; the standing rule is in CLAUDE.md 'The open-items register'
patterns: index row AND its detail file
decisions.rationale: Measurement, OPEN_ITEMS.md:3-5: the register was created after a full-repository sweep found 91 open items scattered across 12 tracking surfaces with 11 status contradictions.

decisions.title: The decisions register records what was decided and its status - nothing else
decisions.verbatim:
**The register holds WHAT WAS DECIDED, and its status. Nothing else.** The proposed
   `conformance` field is REMOVED.
decisions.plain: This decisions register says what was decided and whether it still stands. Whether the code obeys it is tracked separately, in the open-items register, because those two things change on different clocks.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-208.md:46-67 (SHAPE RATIFIED, three rulings)
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, open_items/OI-208.md:49-54 (the user's recorded rationale): a decision's status changes only when someone rules again, whereas whether the code obeys it changes every time the code moves. Holding both in one row produces a register that silently goes stale - the exact failure the issue register was created to end.

decisions.title: A decision belongs in the owning layer's specification; the register is an index
decisions.verbatim:
**A decision belongs, wherever possible, in the OWNING LAYER'S SPECIFICATION** — that layer's
   section of `ARCHITECTURE.md` — and the register is the **index and pointer**, never a
   substitute home.
decisions.plain: A decision about how a stage should work is written into that stage's part of the architecture document. This decisions register only points at it.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-208.md:46-67; follows the CLAUDE.md Conventions rule of 2026-07-28
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, open_items/OI-208.md:55-62: the layer specification is where a reader looks for how a layer should work, so a register that held the decision instead of pointing at it would become a second home (#6) and the specification would stay silent.

decisions.title: Never work from memory instead of documented facts
decisions.verbatim:
No assertion, design, decision, dispatch or report may rest on recalled or
  inferred content when a documented source exists. Open the primary source and cite it
  (file:line).
decisions.plain: If a document records something, read it and quote it rather than remembering it. Being right from memory does not count, because correct memory and incorrect memory look the same until you check.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md Conventions, user-directed 2026-07-28; its founding instance is the Layer-2 note-collection reading that this adjudication's method is built to prevent
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` Conventions, with its founding instance recorded there: correct memory is indistinguishable from incorrect memory without checking, and the check is what surfaces the parts the memory did not contain - on 2026-07-28 the Layer-2 specification turned out to state explicitly and twice what had been reported as ambiguous.

decisions.title: Music-theory words are reserved for their music-theory meaning
decisions.verbatim:
Any term that coincides even slightly with music theory is used
  ONLY in its musical sense.
decisions.plain: In this project a score is a piece of music, a key is a tonality, and a measure is a bar. Where a word is needed in its everyday computing sense, it must be qualified - candidate score, map key, measurement.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md Conventions, user-directed 2026-07-28; open_items/OI-229 records the convention STANDING for new writing and the tree-wide cleanup as an unratified future work item
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` Conventions, user-directed 2026-07-28: this is a music-analysis system, so an ambiguous domain vocabulary makes every document harder to read and every specification easier to misapply.

decisions.title: The decoder commits its best path; there is no abstention on the key axis
decisions.verbatim: **key-abstain 0** — A commits its MAP path, the OI-33 flag reads zero
decisions.plain: The joint estimator always names a key. It never declines to answer on the key axis, so the abstention counter is always zero.

decisions.title: The regression stop is the granularity-robust unit; root governs, key and Roman numeral ride beside
decisions.verbatim:
the **class-(b) (pitch-class-decidable-root) root-disagree DURATION
  must be NON-INCREASING** vs the committed reference — the *meaningful* functional errors never grow.
decisions.plain: A change is allowed to ship only if the total amount of music on which we name the wrong chord root - counted where the root is decidable at all - does not grow. The key and the Roman numeral are watched alongside but do not govern.

decisions.title: The system is a module inside MuseScore Studio, not a plugin
decisions.verbatim:
This system is implemented as a new module (`composing`) within MuseScore Studio's
existing C++ codebase. It is not a plugin. It integrates directly with MuseScore's
score model, rendering pipeline, playback engine, and UI infrastructure.
decisions.plain: The harmonic analysis is built into MuseScore Studio's own program code as a new component of it, not added on afterwards as a plugin. It uses MuseScore's own score model, engraving, playback and interface directly.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:370-374: the analysis library itself has NO engraving dependency and is pure music theory; the bridge layer is what touches the engraving model. Being a module rather than a plugin is what lets that bridge exist at all.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:322-326 (§1.2). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The long-term intent is an official contribution to MuseScore Studio
decisions.verbatim:
The long-term intent is for this to become an official contribution to MuseScore Studio.
All code follows MuseScore's coding standards, licensing requirements, and contribution
guidelines.
decisions.plain: The aim is for this work eventually to become part of MuseScore Studio proper, so it is written to MuseScore's own coding, licensing and contribution rules from the start.
decisions.rationale: Derivation not recorded for the intent itself. What the record does state is the consequence it carries (ARCHITECTURE.md:329-330): following MuseScore's standards from the start is what keeps the contribution possible.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:328-330 (§1.2); restated at ARCHITECTURE.md:6454-6456 (the composing module is 'intended as a future contribution'). ★ READ WITH the CLAUDE.md DISTRIBUTION CONSTRAINT (D-197): the MusicXML declared-mode import patch cfc7eb5e39 is FORK-LOCAL ONLY and must NEVER reach musescore/MuseScore. Two recorded positions - a general intent and a one-patch exception - and the record does not state how the general intent applies to the rest of the tree.

decisions.title: GPL v3, and every external library must be GPL v3 compatible
decisions.verbatim:
All code is licensed under **GPL v3** — consistent with MuseScore Studio's open source
license. All external libraries used must be GPL v3 compatible.
decisions.plain: All the code is released under the GPL v3 licence, the same licence MuseScore Studio uses, and no outside library may be used unless its licence is compatible with that.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:334-335: consistency with MuseScore Studio's own open source licence. A GPL-incompatible library would make the code undistributable with MuseScore.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:332-335 (§1.3). No date or ratifier stated. The per-file consequence is ARCHITECTURE.md:6287 - a GPL v3 header on every file.

decisions.title: The MuseScore contributor licence agreement is signed before any pull request
decisions.verbatim:
The Contributor License Agreement (CLA) with MuseScore must be signed before any
pull requests are submitted.
decisions.plain: Before any of this work is offered back to MuseScore as a pull request, the contributor agreement with MuseScore must be signed.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:337-338 (§1.3), restated at ARCHITECTURE.md:6383-6385 (§18.3). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: MuseScore's coding style is followed, with clang-format run before every commit
decisions.verbatim:
Follow MuseScore's existing coding style throughout:
- Formatting defined in `.clang-format` — run clang-format before every commit
- Naming conventions — consistent with existing MuseScore code
- File headers — GPL v3 license header on every file (see existing files for template)
- Include ordering — follow MuseScore's convention
decisions.plain: The code looks like MuseScore's own code: the formatter configuration in the repository is run before every commit, names follow MuseScore's conventions, every file carries the GPL v3 header, and includes are ordered MuseScore's way.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:467-471 (§2.8): read how MuseScore already does a thing and follow the same pattern rather than inventing parallel infrastructure - the same reason that governs panels, score traversal, playback, settings and localization.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6282-6288 (§17.1). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Where MuseScore's documentation practice is minimal, the higher standard applies
decisions.verbatim: Where MuseScore's documentation practice is minimal, use good practice instead.
decisions.plain: Following MuseScore's conventions does not mean copying how little it documents. Where MuseScore documents sparsely, this project documents properly instead.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6342-6345 (§17.3): the analyzers are the most complex components in the codebase, and a musician with reasonable theoretical knowledge must be able to read them and understand why each decision was made.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6282-6290 (§17.1). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Every public class and method is documented in musical terms
decisions.verbatim:
Every public class must have a documentation comment explaining:
- What musical concept it implements
- What it receives as input (in musical terms)
- What it produces as output (in musical terms)
- What it does not handle (important for setting expectations)
decisions.plain: A public class must say which musical idea it implements, what music it takes in, what it produces, and what it deliberately does not handle. A public method must say the same about the musical operation it performs, in musical terms rather than programming terms.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:452-456 (§2.6) with :6322-6323: the documentation is written so a person with reasonable musical knowledge and basic programming familiarity can read it, including MuseScore contributors with no familiarity with this codebase at all.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6292-6304 (§17.2). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: public class must have a documentation comment

decisions.title: Every non-obvious scoring weight or threshold explains its musical reasoning
decisions.verbatim: Every non-obvious scoring weight or threshold must explain its musical reasoning.
decisions.plain: A number in the scoring code that is not self-evident must be accompanied by the musical reason it has the value it has.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6342-6345 (§17.3): the analyzers are the most complex components, and their weights and thresholds are where the musical judgment actually lives - an undocumented one is unreadable and unarguable.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6306 (§17.2). No date or ratifier stated. ★ This is the rule the 2026-08-01 CLAUDE.md Conventions entry generalizes from scoring values to design decisions as a class (D-195) - and the rule this register's rationale field serves.

decisions.title: The analyzer code must be readable by a musician
decisions.verbatim:
Every scoring weight, threshold, and heuristic must be documented with its musical
rationale. A musician with reasonable theoretical knowledge must be able to read the
analyzer code and understand why each decision was made.
decisions.plain: Every weight, threshold and rule of thumb in the chord and key analyzers carries its musical reason, to the standard that a musician with ordinary theoretical training can read the code and see why each choice was made.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6342: these are the most complex components in the codebase, so they are where readability is worth the most.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6340-6352 (§17.3), which gives a worked example from existing code (the circle-of-fifths interval deltas). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Every test documents the musical situation, the expected result, and what a failure means
decisions.verbatim:
Every test must document:
- What musical situation is being tested
- What the expected result is and why it is musically correct
- What a failure would indicate about the system's behavior
decisions.plain: A test says which musical situation it exercises, what the right answer is and why it is musically right, and what it would mean about the system if the test failed.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6361-6362: the tests must be readable by MuseScore contributors with no deep familiarity with this codebase.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6354-6362 (§17.4). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: One coherent piece of functionality per pull request
decisions.verbatim:
Each pull request should implement one coherent piece of functionality. Large
pull requests are hard to review. The phased plan in Section 15 defines natural
PR boundaries.
decisions.plain: Each contribution offered back to MuseScore does one thing.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6377-6379: large pull requests are hard to review, and the phased plan defines where the natural boundaries fall.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6375-6379 (§18.2). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: An architectural decision that changes is documented in the same commit
decisions.verbatim:
When an architectural decision changes — update this document in the same commit.
Stale documentation is worse than no documentation because it actively misleads.
Claude Code should update relevant sections of this document as its last act when
a session changes an architectural decision.
decisions.plain: When a design decision changes, the change to this document goes in the same commit as the change to the code.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6390: stale documentation is worse than no documentation, because it actively misleads.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6387-6392 (§18.4); the standing principle is CLAUDE.md #10 (D-174). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: update this document in the same commit

decisions.title: Styles are defined entirely in data; adding one never requires code changes
decisions.verbatim:
Musical styles are defined entirely in JSON files. The C++ code implements mechanisms —
voice leading optimization, chord generation, voicing rules — while JSON files define
parameters. Adding a new style never requires C++ changes.
decisions.plain: A musical style is a data file. The program code implements the mechanisms - voice leading, chord generation, voicing - and the style file supplies the numbers that make one style behave differently from another. Adding a style is never a code change.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:388-390 (§2.1) with the worked wrong/correct pair at :392-402: behaviour that branched on a style's identity would make every new or renamed style a code change.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4023-4027 (§6.1); the principle it realizes is D-070 (§2.1). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: styles are defined entirely in JSON

decisions.title: Style conflicts resolve by a declared priority - explicit overrides always win
decisions.verbatim:
**Conflict resolution priority:**
1. System defaults — lowest priority
2. Mixin sources — in declared order, later overrides earlier
3. Explicit `overrides` in the style file — highest priority, always wins
decisions.plain: When a style assembles itself from several inherited sources, the order of precedence is fixed: system defaults are weakest, inherited sources come next in the order they are declared with later ones winning, and anything the style file states explicitly wins outright.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4069-4072 (§6.2). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The style loader never names a style in code
decisions.verbatim:
The style loader scans the styles directory recursively and loads all valid JSON files.
It never references specific style IDs in code — it simply loads whatever it finds.
decisions.plain: The loader reads whatever style files it finds in the styles directory. No style's name appears anywhere in the program code.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:435-438 (§2.4): no comparison against a style name anywhere in the codebase - style-specific behaviour flows entirely through parameters.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4103-4106 (§6.4); the principle it realizes is D-070 (§2.1/§2.4). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: One shared style taxonomy, not two parallel vocabularies
decisions.verbatim:
The style vocabulary the presets select on is **one shared, hierarchical taxonomy** (common-practice / jazz / vernacular
families — Baroque, Classical/galant, Romantic; trad, swing/songbook, bebop, hard-bop, cool, modal; blues, ragtime,
gospel-soul, rock, pop, folk, barbershop) — the **same** set the Harmonic Vocabulary (§7) tags its entries with, not two
parallel vocabularies. Inclusion rule: a style is listed iff it has a **distinct functional-harmonic vocabulary** (free
jazz / atonal excluded).
decisions.plain: The list of style families the presets choose from is the SAME list the harmonic vocabulary tags its entries with - one hierarchy, not two that can drift apart. A style earns a place on it only if its functional harmony is genuinely distinct, which is why free jazz and atonal music are not on it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4153-4155 - #6, one path per concern, applied to a vocabulary: two parallel taxonomies of the same thing would diverge, and the inclusion rule (a distinct functional-harmonic vocabulary) is what keeps the list from growing by analogy.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4149-4159 (§6.7); full proposal `cowork_progression_schema_dictionary.md` §6/§12 and `cowork_style_clustering_plan.md`. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The style taxonomy is a theory-based first version; grounding it empirically is committed work
decisions.verbatim:
It is a **theory-based v1**; **empirically grounding** it — deriving the clusters *and* the
per-style weights by clustering corpora — is committed future work (`cowork_style_clustering_plan.md`)
decisions.plain: The style families and their weights are currently drawn from music theory, not from data. Deriving both from corpora instead is recorded as work that will be done, not as an option.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4156-4158: the clusters and their feature distributions are one data-derived object, and it is reachable for jazz and pop from lead-sheet corpora even where note-level ground truth is scarce - which is what makes the grounding committable rather than aspirational.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4149-4159 (§6.7). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The harmonic vocabulary is a queried reference component, not a layer of the analysis
decisions.verbatim:
It is reference knowledge **queried** by the layers and by
future tools, **not a pipeline layer**. Entries carry **provenance** (established theory), not a ground-truth-validation
status — validation is the *consumer's* concern (verifiability contract, §2.15).
decisions.plain: The catalogue of progressions and substitutions is something the analysis stages ask questions of, not a stage they pass through. Its entries say where the theory comes from; whether that theory holds up against real music is the caller's question, not the catalogue's.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4177 - the verifiability contract (D-029): reference knowledge grounded in established theory may be carried without corpus validation, provided the consumer that puts it under load is the one that must validate it.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4168-4182 (§7); own specification `cowork_progression_schema_dictionary.md`. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: A voicing type is never requested directly; the style selects it
decisions.verbatim:
// Style determines which voicing types are used and in what proportion.
    // Never call with a specific voicing type directly — encode that in the style.
decisions.plain: A caller asking for a voicing says which style it wants, never which voicing technique. The style decides whether the answer is a drop-2, a shell, a chorale spacing or something else, and in what proportion.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4273-4276: keeping the interface voicing-type agnostic is what lets a new voicing type be added as a generator implementation plus a style parameter, without the interface changing.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4268-4290 (§8.2); the principle it realizes is D-070 (§2.1). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: never call with a specific voicing type

decisions.title: A fixed element is a hard constraint the optimizer may never modify
decisions.verbatim:
Fixed elements are hard constraints in the voice leading optimizer — they anchor
the dynamic programming search. The optimizer guarantees never modifying them.
decisions.plain: Anything the user has pinned - a note, a voice, a chord, a passage - anchors the search for good voice leading. The optimizer works around it and never changes it.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4412-4451 (§9.1-§9.2). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: hard constraints in the voice leading optimizer

decisions.title: The inference demo view is a developer tool and is not shipped
decisions.verbatim:
A step-through visualization of the inference pipeline, for use by developers
during quality assurance and algorithmic development. Not shipped to end users.
decisions.plain: The step-by-step view of the analysis making its decisions exists so a developer can watch and judge it by eye and ear. It is not part of what a user gets.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4469-4471: it exists to make musical correctness checkable by eye and ear rather than only through the automated agreement numbers.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4463-4553 (§10.0), whose own status line reads 'Not yet started'. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The harmony maps are our own visual design, and are chosen partly to avoid intellectual-property claims
decisions.verbatim:
MTH Pro-style map based on Berklee chord-scale theory (Nettles, Levine). Positions
chords by functional region (tonic, subdominant, dominant) and shows available
tensions. Our own visual design — not a reproduction of MTH Pro's specific layout.
decisions.plain: The planned map of harmonic function draws on published chord-scale theory but is laid out our own way, not copied from the commercial product that inspired it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4598 and :4573: the circle of fifths and the Tonnetz were chosen partly because they carry no intellectual-property claim - the Tonnetz being a nineteenth-century mathematical structure - and the same reasoning is what forces an original layout for the functional map.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4595-4618 (§10.2-§10.4), all three marked planned. No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: not a reproduction of MTH Pro

decisions.title: Chord preview uses MuseScore's note-input pathway, not the playback pipeline
decisions.verbatim:
**Implementation note:** Use MuseScore's note-input preview pathway (same as hearing
a note when clicking in input mode) — not the full score playback pipeline. The
full pipeline has too much latency for interactive map exploration. Inference runs
on a background thread via `QtConcurrent` to keep the UI responsive.
decisions.plain: Clicking a chord on a harmony map plays it through the same quick path MuseScore uses when you hear a note as you enter it, not through full score playback.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4648-4650: the full playback pipeline has too much delay for interactive exploration, and the inference runs on a background thread so the interface stays responsive.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4620-4650 (§10.5), a planned component. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The language model holds no object references - every tool call carries its own musical address
decisions.verbatim:
**Stateless tool-call model.** The LLM does not hold object references. Each
tool call carries its own musical address. No proxy objects, no EID handles,
no lifecycle management. This is the right model for LLM interaction and the
simpler one to implement.
decisions.plain: When a language model asks the program to do something, it names the place in the music each time. It never holds a handle to an object in the score.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6422-6423: no proxy objects, no element handles and no lifecycle management - recorded as both the right model for this kind of interaction and the simpler one to implement.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6413-6423 (§19.2), a planned module; full design `docs/llm_integration.md`. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The language model is a search agent and is never given the whole score
decisions.verbatim:
**LLM as search agent.** The LLM is never given a full score dump. It has
search tools (`find_notes`, `get_part`, `get_measure`, `search_harmony`) and
fetches what it needs iteratively — exactly as Claude Code uses Grep and Read
in a large codebase. Serialization quality is the critical foundation: clean,
hierarchical, beat-aligned, free of layout noise.
decisions.plain: Rather than being handed the entire score, the language model is given tools to find what it needs and fetches it piece by piece - the way a person reads a large document by searching it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6428-6429: because the model reads what it fetches, the quality of that serialization - clean, hierarchical, beat-aligned, free of layout noise - is the critical foundation.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6413-6429 (§19.2), a planned module. No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: never given a full score dump

decisions.title: The language model sees what the user set, not what the engraving engine derived
decisions.verbatim:
**Intentional vs. computed.** The LLM sees everything the user deliberately
set (pitch, dynamics, articulation, note color, lyrics formatting, visibility).
It does not see what the engraving engine derived (positions, beam geometry,
stem lengths, `LayoutData`). The `Pid` property system is the practical
boundary.
decisions.plain: The model is shown the composer's own choices - pitches, dynamics, articulation, colour, lyrics, visibility - and not the results of laying the music out, such as positions, beam geometry or stem lengths.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6435: MuseScore's own property system is the practical boundary between the two, so the split is enforceable rather than judged case by case.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6413-6435 (§19.2), a planned module. No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: does not see what the engraving engine derived

decisions.title: The composing module is the language model's context provider; the model never re-derives harmony
decisions.verbatim:
The composing module (`src/composing/`) is the LLM's context provider. Its
harmonic analysis output (chord symbols, Roman numerals, key inference,
harmonic rhythm) is included in every score section sent to the LLM. The LLM
does not re-derive harmony from raw pitch data — it receives pre-digested
musical context.
decisions.plain: Every stretch of music sent to a language model arrives with our harmonic analysis already attached - chord symbols, Roman numerals, key, harmonic rhythm. The model reads that; it does not work the harmony out from the notes itself.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6450-6452: the same analysis also drives the validation step that checks voice leading and harmonic consistency before a generated change reaches the score, so one analysis serves both directions.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6442-6456 (§19.3), a planned module. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The language-model bridge is built as a module but confined to the core access layer, so it can become a plugin
decisions.verbatim:
**Build strategy:** Implement the LLM bridge as a native module initially for
speed, but strictly constrained to the Core Access Layer only (never bypassing
it to the DOM). When the plugin API matures, migration to a plugin is then
straightforward. See `docs/llm_integration.md §11` for the full argument.
decisions.plain: It is written inside the program for speed of development, but restricted to the same narrow interface a plugin would have, so that moving it out to a plugin later is straightforward.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6458-6463: with a properly designed plugin interface the bridge does not need to live in the core at all - it becomes optional, independently updatable, provider-agnostic and open to community alternatives - so the constraint is what keeps that end state reachable.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6458-6468 (§19.4), a planned module; full argument `docs/llm_integration.md` §11. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Percussion is excluded from analysis and tuning; fixed-pitch instruments are the tuning anchor
decisions.verbatim:
Percussion instruments are excluded from both harmonic analysis and intonation.
Fixed-pitch instruments (piano) serve as intonation anchors when present.
decisions.plain: Unpitched percussion takes no part in working out the harmony and receives no tuning adjustment. Where a piano or organ is playing, the other instruments tune to it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4675-4676 and :4781-4782: a fixed-pitch instrument cannot adjust, so it is the natural reference - and its presence resets accumulated drift at every chord it plays.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4669-4689 (§11.2). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: One preference chooses the tuning system, and no tuning code hardcodes one
decisions.verbatim:
All tuning code paths read the preference at call time via `preferredTuningSystem()`
(defined in `notationtuningbridge.cpp`), which resolves the key through
`TuningRegistry::byKey()` with a `JustIntonation` fallback if the key is unset or
unknown.  No tuning code hardcodes a specific system.
decisions.plain: Which tuning system is in force is a single user setting, read afresh each time any tuning happens. No part of the tuning code has a system built into it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4691-4699 - #6, one path per concern: the same preference governs per-note tuning, chord-staff population and region tuning, so the three cannot silently disagree about what tuning the user asked for.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4691-4707 (§11.2a). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: A tie chain is one indivisible tuning event, and its tuning comes from one authority note
decisions.verbatim:
**Tied notes:** A non-partial tie chain explicitly carries a compositional instruction of
continuity. For region tuning, the entire non-partial tie chain is treated as one tuning
event. The chain must not be split. Its tuning is set from a single authority note and
protected thereafter; later harmonic regions tune around that established pitch.
decisions.plain: Notes joined by ties are one sustained sound, so they are tuned once and never split apart. The tuning is worked out from a single note in the chain - the one carrying a tuning anchor if there is one, otherwise the first - and applied unchanged to the whole chain.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4950-4951 and :4923-4924: a tie is a compositional instruction of continuity, so splitting it would contradict what the composer wrote; a user who wants the sustained sound retuned as the harmony moves writes a slur instead.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4950-4963 (§11.3c), with the region-tuning consequence at :5726-5729 (§11.6). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: A slur, not a tie, joins the halves of a split note
decisions.verbatim:
A **slur** (not a tie) connects the two halves.  This is a deliberate choice:
MuseScore's playback engine treats tied notes as one continuous sound with a single
tuning value, so a tie would silently discard note_B's tuning.  A slur produces two
independent playback events with legato articulation, allowing each half to carry
its own tuning offset.
decisions.plain: When a sustained note must be retuned partway through, it is cut in two and the halves are joined with a slur rather than a tie.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5390-5393: MuseScore's playback treats tied notes as one continuous sound with a single tuning value, so a tie would silently discard the second half's tuning; a slur produces two independent playback events, each able to carry its own offset.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5382-5393 (§11.4). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The split is visible in the score; the invisible alternative is deferred
decisions.verbatim:
The split is **visible** — the score shows two shorter notes connected by a slur.
This is the simplest correct approach and is fully undoable via MuseScore's standard
undo system.
decisions.plain: The reader sees two shorter notes joined by a slur where a note was retuned. The alternative - keeping the written note and hiding a silent playing copy - was designed and set aside.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5396-5397: the visible split is the simplest correct approach and is fully undoable through MuseScore's own undo. The excluded alternative's recorded blocker (:5360-5363) is that it needs a visual indicator for tuning-applied notes before it is practical.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5395-5402 (§11.4), with the deferred alternative recorded at `backlog_invisible_split.md`. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Only visible, sounding notes enter the pitch-class collection
decisions.verbatim:
Chord analysis filters notes with `visible = true` and `play = true`, excluding
both silent notes and any future invisible tuning artifacts from the pitch-class
collection.
decisions.plain: Notes marked invisible, and notes that do not play, take no part in identifying the chord - which also keeps any hidden note created by the tuning machinery out of the analysis.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5420-5421: the filter excludes both silent notes and any future invisible tuning artifact, so tuning a passage cannot change what the analysis of that passage sees.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5417-5421 (§11.4). No date or ratifier stated. The joint estimator's own eligibility flags are the Layer-1 fact surface (D-039/D-045).

decisions.title: The chord staff is the output, never an input to the analysis that fills it
decisions.verbatim:
The target staff is excluded from the analysis input — it is the output, not a
source.  This prevents feedback loops when re-running the analysis.
decisions.plain: When the harmonic reduction is written onto a staff, that staff's own contents are kept out of the analysis that produced them.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5477: it prevents a feedback loop when the analysis is re-run over music that already carries its own reduction. The joint estimator's record path realizes the same rule at its own input surface - D-013, open_items/OI-204.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5467-5477 (§11.5). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: target staff is excluded from the analysis input

decisions.title: Populating the chord staff overwrites whatever is in the selected range
decisions.verbatim:
**Any existing content in the selected region is overwritten.**  Re-analysis after
score edits simply selects the same range and runs again.  If the user wants to
preserve a previous analysis, they can undo or copy it elsewhere first.
decisions.plain: Running the reduction again over the same passage replaces what is there. Keeping an earlier analysis is the user's job - undo it, or copy it somewhere else first.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5479-5481 (§11.5). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: existing content in the selected region is overwritten

decisions.title: Roman numerals and Nashville numbers are never shown together on one staff
decisions.verbatim:
**Chord function notation** attached below the treble staff — either
`HarmonyType::ROMAN` (Roman numerals) or `HarmonyType::NASHVILLE` (Nashville
numbers), selected by the "Chord function notation" preference (None / Roman
numerals / Nashville numbers).  Roman and Nashville are mutually exclusive on
the staff because they encode identical information; displaying both would be
redundant and legibility-destroying.
decisions.plain: The chord staff shows one or the other beneath the music, chosen by preference, never both.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5544-5546: the two notations encode identical information, so showing both would be redundant and would destroy legibility.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5541-5546 (§11.5); the same choice on the analysis side is D-086. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Interactive annotations are written in the score's normal colour; the batch pipeline writes red
decisions.verbatim:
Interactive annotate path (human use): annotations written in score default
color (black). Publication-ready, indistinguishable from manually entered
symbols. No user preference exposed.

Automated pipeline (`batch_analyze` headless): annotations written in red,
hardcoded in `tools/batch_analyze.cpp`. Never exposed to human user. Used by
`auto_review.py` to filter our inferred annotations from pre-existing score
content by color comparison.
decisions.plain: When a person runs the annotation, what it writes looks like anything else they typed. When the headless batch tool runs it, everything it writes is red.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5733-5739: the interactive output is meant to be publication-ready and indistinguishable from hand-entered symbols, while the red is a filter criterion that lets the automated review separate our inferred annotations from whatever the score already contained.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5730-5739 (§11.5). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: New panels use MuseScore's own panel and interface infrastructure
decisions.verbatim:
New panels follow MuseScore's existing panel architecture — KDDockWidgets for
panel management, QML for UI components. Do not create parallel infrastructure.
Read how existing MuseScore panels are implemented before creating new ones.
decisions.plain: Any new panel is built with the same window-docking and interface technology MuseScore already uses, after reading how MuseScore's existing panels are built. No parallel machinery is created.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:467-471 (§2.8): read how MuseScore already does it and follow the same pattern - the same rule that governs score traversal, playback, settings and localization.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5848-5852 (§12.1); the panels themselves are planned (§12.2-§12.5). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Every user-visible string goes through MuseScore's localization, in English and Swedish
decisions.verbatim:
All user-visible strings use MuseScore's existing Qt localization infrastructure
(`.ts` files, Qt Linguist). English and Swedish translations provided for all new strings.
decisions.plain: Text a user can read is translatable through MuseScore's own translation system, and every new string is supplied in English and Swedish.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5854-5855 (§12.1); listed in the Core scope at ARCHITECTURE.md:6250-6251. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Accessibility follows MuseScore's existing patterns
decisions.verbatim:
Accessibility follows MuseScore's existing Qt accessibility patterns — focus
management, keyboard navigation, screen reader hooks.
decisions.plain: Keyboard navigation, focus handling and screen-reader support are done the way MuseScore already does them.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5857-5858 (§12.1); listed in the Core scope at ARCHITECTURE.md:6251. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The harmonic-display preference exists for clarity, not for cost
decisions.verbatim:
A user preference controls whether harmonic analysis is shown in the status bar. This
preference exists for UI clarity — some users find the chord and key information
distracting, particularly when doing work unrelated to harmony. It is not a performance
control: analysis cost is negligible (well under 1ms) and suppressing the display does
not require skipping the analysis.
decisions.plain: The setting that hides the harmonic information from the status bar is there because some users find it distracting, not because the analysis is expensive. Switching it off does not skip the analysis.
decisions.rationale: Measurement named in the record, ARCHITECTURE.md:5864-5866: the analysis cost at this seam is 'well under 1ms'. ★ That number is the LEGACY bounded-window path's; open_items/OI-203 and OI-206 record the record arm running a whole-score decode per selection, measured in seconds on large scores - so the reason this preference is not a performance control no longer holds as stated.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5860-5870 (§12.1a). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Our data lives in separate files inside the score archive; the score file is never touched
decisions.verbatim:
MuseScore's MSCZ format is a ZIP archive. Our metadata lives as additional files
within the archive alongside `score.mscx`:
decisions.plain: Constraints, branches, cached analysis and preferences travel with the score as extra files inside its archive, beside the standard MuseScore score file, which our code never modifies.
decisions.rationale: Stated trade-off, ARCHITECTURE.md:5940-5944: the score stays a valid standard MuseScore file with zero interference in MuseScore's own reading and writing, and our data travels with it. The accepted cost is stated too - exporting to MusicXML, PDF or MIDI loses it, which is acceptable because the workflow is MuseScore-native.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5926-5944 (§13.1), a planned component. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Every custom file carries a format version, and the score file is never rewritten by our persistence
decisions.verbatim:
All our custom files include a format version field. When the format changes,
migration code handles existing files. The score.mscx is never modified by our
persistence layer.
decisions.plain: Each of our own files records which version of its format it is, so older files can be migrated when the format changes; the standard MuseScore score file inside the archive is never rewritten by us.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5946-5950 (§13.2), a planned component. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Arranger interactions are logged from the start, with consent, as future training data
decisions.verbatim:
The system logs arranger interactions from the start — with user consent — as
future ML training data. Every suggestion accepted, modified, or rejected is a
labeled training example specific to vocal jazz arranging, filling the corpus gap
identified in the design phase.
decisions.plain: Every suggestion a user accepts, changes or rejects is recorded - with their consent - as a labelled example for future machine learning.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5993-5994: the recording exists to fill the corpus gap identified in the design phase, there being no existing labelled corpus of vocal jazz arranging decisions.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5989-6006 (§14.2), a planned component. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Chord symbols already in a score are a second analyst's opinion, not ground truth
decisions.verbatim:
Mode 2 — Pre-existing symbols present: treated as a second analyst's opinion,
not ground truth. Judge comments on agreements and disagreements without
scoring disagreements as errors. Framing: "two analysts may reach different
but equally valid conclusions."
decisions.plain: When the automated review meets a score that already carries chord symbols, it treats them as another analyst's reading. Disagreements are discussed, not scored as our errors.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6025-6026, in the record's own words: two analysts may reach different but equally valid conclusions. Errors are scored only in Mode 3, against a known ground-truth corpus (:5989-5990) - the same distinction the project's standing rule draws between corroboration and ground truth.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6008-6033 (§14, the automated annotation review), marked planned. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The development tools are not part of the shipping product
decisions.verbatim:
The following tools live in `tools/` and are **not part of the shipping product**.
They are compiled/run only in development builds (`MUE_BUILD_ENGRAVING_DEVTOOLS=ON`).
decisions.plain: The batch analysis tool, the comparison scripts and the remaining measurement tools are built only in development builds and never ship to a user.

and `iex_musicxml` — no notation module required. Because the tool only consumes

decisions.title: What is out of scope, and what degrades gracefully at the boundary
decisions.verbatim:
Live and real-time operation, film synchronization, adaptive game music, non-Western
traditions (graceful degradation at boundary), post-tonal and serial music (graceful
degradation at boundary), audio transcription from recording, spatial music, extended
techniques as primary language.
decisions.plain: Live performance, film and game synchronization, audio transcription, spatial music and extended techniques as a primary language are not attempted. Non-Western traditions and post-tonal music are not attempted either, but the system is required to fail gracefully where it meets them rather than producing confident nonsense.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6238-6276 (§16), which sorts the whole feature set into Core / Important / Prepared / Out of scope. No date or ratifier stated.

   published research, public algorithms, public software. Fact-finding (investigative)

decisions.plain: Nothing is built on a hunch. Every method comes from published research, a public algorithm, or public software. Investigating to find out what the facts are is a separate, permitted activity.

decisions.title: #17 - the Premise Gate
decisions.verbatim:
17. **The Premise Gate.** Before any inference-affecting design is built or probed:
    (a) a **premise ledger** — every load-bearing causal claim explicitly labeled **FACT**
    (citation to code/measurement), **THEORY** (citation to published research answering the
    *specific* question, #2), or **ASSUMPTION**; (b) a **written quantitative prediction per
    assumption** (fire-rate, magnitude, direction, population) recorded *before* measuring —
    no prediction, no build; (c) a **desk simulation** — trace the mechanism by hand through
    the intended architecture on 3–5 real corpus cases drawn from the known failing sets,
    answering FIRST "does the mechanism FIRE on this case?" (control flow — ratified sharpening
    2026-07-10, the EG-2 desk-sim lesson), THEN "which term moves, by how much?" (arithmetic);
    (d) every **proxy→target
    link is itself a ledger premise** (a structural proxy never stands in for a behavioral
    quantity unvalidated); (e) every **insulation claim** ("X cannot affect Y") must enumerate
    the false-negative path explicitly; (f) **no hand-transcribed measurement numbers** —
    figures enter docs only via generated artifacts (the `manifest.json` pattern).
decisions.plain: Before anything that affects the analysis is built or even probed: every load-bearing causal claim is written down and labelled as an established fact, a published theory, or an assumption; every assumption gets a written numerical prediction BEFORE anything is measured; the mechanism is traced by hand through three to five real failing cases, asking first whether it fires at all and only then what it changes; any stand-in quantity must itself be justified; any claim that one thing cannot affect another must name how it could; and no number enters a document by being typed in by hand.
decisions.rationale: Measurement, CLAUDE.md:44-45: part (c)'s fire-first ordering is a ratified sharpening from a specific failure - the desk simulation that traced arithmetic through a mechanism which, on the real case, never fired. Part (f)'s reason is recorded across the decisions register as the generated-artifact pattern: a hand-transcribed figure cannot be re-derived, and the harvest's own counts drifted one regeneration stale exactly that way.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md:37-50; ratified by the user 2026-07-10, analysis in `cowork_premise_gate_reflection.md` (CLAUDE.md:122-125).

decisions.title: #18 - an unverified causal premise is forbidden (Class A)
decisions.verbatim:
18. **Unverified causal premises are FORBIDDEN (Class A).** No design may carry load on a
    causal claim about our own system or data that is checkable but unchecked.
decisions.plain: No design may rest on a claim about how our own system or data behaves when that claim could be checked and has not been.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:51-52: the prohibition is specifically about claims that are CHECKABLE - the cost of checking is what makes leaving them unchecked indefensible.

decisions.title: #19 - an unestablished measurement tool is forbidden (Class B)
decisions.verbatim:
19. **Unestablished instruments are FORBIDDEN (Class B).** An instrument, corpus, gate, or
    recorded figure is trusted only after being *positively established* (oracle cross-check,
    derivation of what the measurement unit actually measures, reproduce-check) — never
    because it is merely unfalsified.
decisions.plain: A measuring script, a corpus, a gate or a recorded figure is trusted only once it has been positively shown to be right - checked against an independent oracle, with a derivation of what its unit actually measures, and a reproduce-check. Never merely because nothing has contradicted it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:55-56: 'never because it is merely unfalsified' - absence of contradiction is not evidence, so establishment has to be a positive act.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md:53-56; ratified by the user 2026-07-10, analysis in `cowork_premise_gate_reflection.md` (CLAUDE.md:122-125).

decisions.title: #20 - fit and evaluation are separated
decisions.verbatim:
20. **Fit/evaluation separation.** No value is graded on data that helped fit it. Every fit
    event declares its held-out data (split or k-fold) and its capacity budget (parameter
    count, regularization, justified against corpus size) BEFORE fitting; the headline claim
    is the held-out figure. A fitted-and-self-measured number is not established (#19).
decisions.plain: No number is graded on the same music that helped choose it. Before any fitting, the held-back music and the budget of how many free values may be fitted are declared; the headline figure is always the one measured on the held-back music.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:60: a value fitted and then measured on its own fitting data is not established at all (#19) - the figure describes the fitting, not the system.

decisions.title: #21 - ground truth is a measurement tool too, and its accuracy is measured
decisions.verbatim:
21. **Ground truth is an instrument too.** The accuracy of ground truth is itself a measured
    quantity — per-axis annotator agreement, not an assumed binary (sharpens #9's "accurate").
    Every precision target and every "irreducible residual" verdict is interpreted against
    that measured ceiling; without it, structural error and annotator disagreement are
    indistinguishable in the residual.
decisions.plain: How right the reference annotations are is itself something to be measured - how far annotators agree with each other, axis by axis - not assumed. Every precision target and every claim that a remaining error is irreducible is read against that measured ceiling.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:63-65: without the measured ceiling, our own structural error and disagreement between annotators are indistinguishable in what is left over - so an 'irreducible residual' verdict cannot be made at all.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md:61-65; ratified by the user 2026-07-18 (CLAUDE.md:125-129). Sharpens #9.

decisions.title: #22 - every hard gate declares in advance how it handles the largest change it will meet
decisions.verbatim:
22. **Every hard gate carries a pre-declared protocol for the largest change it will face.**
    A gate written only for incremental change must not be amended under the pressure of a
    live diff — the exceptional-event variant (e.g. architecture-scale adoption: aggregate
    criterion + explained diff + snapshot + ratification) is written and ratified before such
    a change is on the table.
decisions.plain: A rule that decides whether a change may ship must say, before the fact, what it does when the change is far bigger than the incremental ones it was written for. It must never be rewritten while such a change is sitting in front of it.

decisions.title: #23 - an end-state principle needs a lawful transition
decisions.verbatim:

    violate an end-state principle (e.g. #6, one path per concern, during a parallel build),
    the violation is declared, bounded, and pre-ratified with a retirement map — migration is
    a first-class state, never an undeclared exception.

decisions.title: #24 - every reported figure carries its uncertainty
decisions.verbatim:
24. **Every reported figure carries its uncertainty.** Sampling noise on the measurement
    corpus is quantified; a difference within the uncertainty is not a finding, and no
    decision rests on one. (The companion of #16: reproducibility bounds instrument error,
    this bounds sampling error.)
decisions.plain: How much a measured number could move by chance, given how much music it was measured on, is quantified and reported with it. A difference inside that range is not a finding and no decision may rest on one.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:77-78: this is the companion of #16 - reproducibility bounds the error the measuring tools introduce, and this bounds the error the sample introduces.

decisions.title: The constrained-optimum ledger corollary
decisions.verbatim:
*Ledger corollary to #17 (ratified with #20–#24):* when a decision selects a **constrained
optimum** (a design chosen for methodology-compliance rather than raw measured performance),
the ledger records what the unconstrained best known alternative is and why it is excluded —
so a future reader can re-test whether the constraint still binds.
decisions.plain: When a design is chosen because it complies with the method rather than because it measured best, the record must name what the best-performing alternative actually was and why it is ruled out.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:82-83: so that a future reader can re-test whether the constraint still binds - without the excluded alternative on record, a constraint that has since been lifted is invisible.

decisions.title: The scope of surprise, and the three-stage funnel
decisions.verbatim:
*Scope of surprise (ratified with #17–19):* surprises are **allowed in explorational runs**
whose purpose is to eliminate ignorance (#5 fact-finding); they are **NOT allowed when building
actual inference code** — there, a surprise is a STOP (#13) and evidence the Premise Gate was
not satisfied. The stage funnel: **desk-simulate (hours) → read-only probe (a session) → build
(an arc)** — each stage kills bad premises before the next pays for them.
decisions.plain: Being surprised is allowed - expected, even - in exploratory work whose whole purpose is to remove ignorance. It is not allowed while building the analysis itself: there a surprise stops the work and shows the Premise Gate was not satisfied. The order of work is: trace it by hand for hours, then probe it read-only for a session, then build it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:89: each stage kills bad premises before the next one pays for them - the funnel is ordered by what a wrong premise costs at that stage.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md:85-89; ratified with #17-#19 by the user 2026-07-10 (CLAUDE.md:122-125).

decisions.title: The decision-neutrality corollary - what exists carries no weight in choosing a design
decisions.verbatim:
*Decision-neutrality of the existing implementation (corollary to #4/#6/#19; user-ratified
2026-07-26):* Designs are chosen from the principles and the ultimate objective — enabling the
best possible inference — alone. In that choice: **(a)** the value of reusing existing code, and
the cost of making existing code obsolete, are SECONDARY — they may break ties between designs
equal under the principles and the objective, and reuse counts only as carried-forward
establishment (#19), never as sunk cost or saved effort; **(b)** downstream implementation
impact — whether and how many consumers must change — carries NO weight; **(c)**
end-user-visible behavior change carries NO weight (the 2026-07-26 unshipped-scoping ruling),
while every behavior change remains ratification-gated (#14) and verification-gated (#15/#19)
exactly as before. The best-possible-inference design is chosen first; what exists then either
serves it or retires. (This does not weaken #6 — one path per concern is an END-STATE structural
principle, not a preservation claim for the existing path; nor #19 — establishment must still
exist before trust.)
decisions.plain: A design is chosen on the principles and the goal of the best possible analysis, and on nothing else. What it would cost to make existing code obsolete is a secondary consideration that can only break a tie between designs already equal; how many places downstream would have to change counts for nothing; and a change in what the user sees counts for nothing either - though every such change still needs ratifying and verifying exactly as before. The best design is chosen first, and what exists then either serves it or is retired.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:110-111 and :116-118: reusing existing code counts only as establishment already carried forward (#19), never as effort saved or cost sunk; and the corollary is explicitly said not to weaken #6 - one path per concern is an end-state structural principle, not a claim that the existing path is the one to preserve.

decisions.title: The two-tier regression class policy - functional regression stops, rotation churn is tracked
decisions.verbatim:
**Two-tier refinement (user-ratified 2026-06-22) — class-(b) functional regression vs class-(a)
symmetric-rotation churn.** A *new* BIR=false case is one of two classes:
- **Class (b) — functional/key regression: UNCHANGED HARD STOP.** A new BIR=false case at a sonority
  whose root is *pitch-class-decidable* (any non-symmetric chord — triads, dominant sevenths, etc.)
  where the analysis now gets the root or key wrong. **Zero** new class-(b) cases on any preset, ever.
  This is the gate's real intent and does not move.
decisions.plain: A newly wrong reading is one of two kinds. If the chord's root is decidable from the notes at all - any ordinary triad or seventh chord - and the analysis now gets the root or the key wrong, that is a functional regression and it is an absolute bar: never one more of them, on any style preset. The other kind is a sonority whose root the notes genuinely cannot decide - a symmetric diminished seventh, an augmented chord, a chord that shares all its notes with another - where no reading is more correct than another by pitch alone. Those are counted and watched, not barred.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:426-431: the pitch-class analyzer is spelling-blind and cannot pick the spelling-correct rotation of a symmetric chord, so counting a rotation flip as a regression would be counting a coin-flip. Measurement bounding the split: on the robust unit the decidable-root class is about 96.5 % of root-fail time (CLAUDE.md:396-399), so the hard stop governs almost all of it. Founding evidence, verified at the score against music21 ground truth: bwv272@4320, bwv289@20160, bwv291@17760, bwv387@10560 (CLAUDE.md:445-448).
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md:411-454, block (B), carried over unchanged to the robust unit at R10-b. Full provenance `cowork_gate_policy_amendment.md`. The four guardrails that make the tracked class conditional - verified at the score per case, default to the barred class on any doubt, the barred class non-increasing, case identities recorded - are at CLAUDE.md:432-441.

decisions.title: A scoring change and its documentation land in the same commit
decisions.verbatim:
**Sync rule — mandatory:** Any commit that adds or modifies a template, bonus,
guard, gate, or other scoring term in `chordanalyzer.cpp` **must** include a
corresponding update to `docs/scoring_model.md` in the same commit. The two
must never drift apart. Specifically:

- Adding a template: update the Templates section (§2), increment the template
  count in the array-size comment, add the guard description if applicable
- Adding or changing a bonus/gate: update the relevant §4 or §6 entry
- Adding a new constraint or dead end: add it to §8

decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:593-598: violating the scoring model's invariants without reading it first has caused several failed attempts, named in the record - the leading-tone ambiguity attempt, four attempts at one bonus, and a rotation-selector bypass. The staleness check is mechanical: the template count in the document must equal the array size in the code (CLAUDE.md:610-613).

decisions.title: Every design decision carries its defense at its home
decisions.verbatim:
- **EVERY DESIGN DECISION CARRIES ITS DEFENSE AT ITS HOME (user-directed, 2026-08-01, at the

  layer's specification in `ARCHITECTURE.md` first — the record states WHY the decision was made:

  constraint that forced it. Every design decision must be defendable, and its defense documented

  as a class. The decisions register (`DECISIONS.md`) points at the defense; where a decision's
  derivation is not in the record, the register says **"derivation not recorded"** — the gap is

  boundary-tick-belongs-to-the-segment-it-starts convention — each recorded with no derivation.
decisions.plain: Wherever a design decision is written down - the owning layer's specification first - the record says WHY: the published research or algorithm it adopts, the measurement that decided it, or the constraint that forced it. Every design decision must be defendable and its defense written where the decision lives. Where the record has none, the decisions register says 'derivation not recorded' rather than supplying one afterwards.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:818-819: this generalizes ARCHITECTURE.md §17.2 - every non-obvious scoring weight or threshold must explain its musical reasoning - from scoring values to design decisions as a class. The reason the gap is stated rather than filled: a defense written after the fact without a source is invention, which the never-work-from-memory rule forbids (CLAUDE.md:822-823).

decisions.title: The self-check: re-read the diff against the principles before reporting

The check is of the work actually on disk, not of the intention — read the diff, not the
memory of writing it. This applies to CC sessions and Cowork sessions alike.

decisions.title: The Windows snap fix in the muse submodule is intentional and must not be reverted
decisions.verbatim:
**File:** `muse/framework/ui/internal/platform/windows/winwindowscontroller.cpp`  
**Function:** `calculateWindowSize()`

Two lines were removed that set `ptMinTrackSize` equal to the full monitor work
area inside the `WM_GETMINMAXINFO` handler. This told Windows the minimum
allowed window size was the entire screen, which prevented Windows Snap from
resizing a maximised MuseScore window into a chosen snap zone (the window
stayed full-screen and lost its title-bar controls).

The fix: `ptMaxSize` and `ptMaxPosition` are kept (they correctly constrain the
maximised position); `ptMinTrackSize` is intentionally left unset.

Upstream issue: musescore/MuseScore#25823 (related cousins: #21344, #16794).  
Introduced by upstream commit `4ad218709` (5 Aug 2025).  
**Do not restore the `ptMinTrackSize` lines.**
decisions.plain: Two lines were removed from MuseScore's Windows window-sizing code that told Windows the smallest allowed window was the whole screen. With them in place, a maximised MuseScore window could not be snapped into a screen zone - it stayed full-screen and lost its title-bar controls. The removal is deliberate and stays.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:651-658: the removed lines set the minimum window size to the full monitor work area, which is what blocked snapping; the maximised-position constraints are correct and are kept. Upstream issue musescore/MuseScore#25823, introduced by upstream commit 4ad218709 (:643-644).

decisions.title: The MusicXML declared-mode import fix is intentional and must not be reverted
decisions.verbatim:
The dedup guarded the `KeySig` creation on **fifths only**:
`if (oldkey != key.key() || key.custom() || key.isAtonal())`. At score start the
prevailing key defaults to `{C, KeyMode::UNKNOWN}` (`KeyList::key()` →
`setConcertKey(Key::C)`), so a **0-fifths** key signature carrying an explicit
`<mode>` (e.g. `<fifths>0</fifths><mode>minor</mode>`) matched the prevailing fifths,
the whole `KeySig` was dropped, and the declared `<mode>` went with it →
`KeyMode::UNKNOWN` downstream. Export *does* write `<mode>`
(`exportmusicxml.cpp:2473`), so this broke export/import round-trip of `<mode>` and,
in our pipeline, dropped the declared-mode anchor on ~79 zero-signature Bach stems
(`cc_key_emission_headroom_dossier.md` — `declaredModeOrdinal=-1`). The maintainers'
own `// TODO only if different custom key ?` flags the dedup as known-incomplete.

The fix: fetch the prevailing `KeySigEvent` (not just the `Key` fifths) and add an
`oldKeySig.mode() != key.mode()` term to the guard, so a mode-bearing key at matching
fifths is retained. A key matching the prevailing one in **both** fifths and mode (and
not custom/atonal) still produces **no** `KeySig`, so plain mode-less C-major scores are
unaffected. Verified isolated to empty-signature scores (exactly 79 zero-sig `.ours.json`
changed, 0 non-empty-signature stems); BIR gate byte-identical on all three presets
(Baroque 57 / Jazz 23 / Default 57); key-inference S2 −378 (Default). Round-trip of
`bwv254` (0-fifths `<mode>minor</mode>`) now preserves `<mode>`.
decisions.plain: MuseScore's importer dropped a key signature that matched the prevailing one in number of sharps or flats even when it declared a different mode - so a piece written with no sharps or flats but marked minor lost that marking on import. The fix compares the mode as well as the accidental count, so a mode-bearing key signature survives.
decisions.rationale: Measurement, CLAUDE.md:685-688: the change is verified isolated to empty-signature scores - exactly 79 zero-signature analyses changed and no non-empty-signature piece moved - the regression gate is byte-identical on all three presets, and the round-trip of a zero-signature minor piece now preserves its mode. The underlying defect is upstream-unchanged code whose own comment flags the check as known-incomplete (CLAUDE.md:678-679, :673-674).
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md:664-694, applied 2026-06-14, commit cfc7eb5e39. ★ Carries the distribution constraint above: fork-local only, never upstream.

decisions.title: Make it work first; compromise on performance only if performance proves a problem
decisions.verbatim:
The user's actual rule: **make it work first (best inference), compromise on performance only if
performance proves to be a problem.** That does not demote runtime speed; it sequences it — and
it means work that makes the same computation faster costs nothing on any principle axis and must
be exhausted BEFORE anything that trades precision for speed. The effort dial and the extent
question are **last resorts, not first ones**.
decisions.plain: Getting the analysis right comes first. Speed is traded against it only once slowness has actually turned out to be a problem. That does not make speed unimportant - it puts it second: anything that makes the same computation faster is free on every principle and is done first, and the settings that buy speed by giving up precision are the last resort, not the first.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, cowork_handoff.md:361-364: work that makes the same computation faster costs nothing on any principle axis, so it must be exhausted BEFORE anything that trades precision for speed - which is what sequences the effort dial and the analysis-extent question last rather than demoting them.
decisions.status_source: cowork_handoff.md:358-364, the user's rulings at the analysis-cost session, 2026-07-28; recorded again as a standing rule at cowork_handoff.md:227-228. It corrects a Cowork misreading of 'implementation efficiency is not very relevant', which meant BUILD effort, not runtime.

decisions.title: A human acts as ground truth where no formal ground truth exists
